title: Chunk without cutting the answer
subtitle: Chunk size, overlap and the sentence that falls in between
mission: Split Aurora’s handbook into chunks for the index. Big chunks mix topics and waste tokens; small ones cut the answer in half. Find a size and overlap where the answer sentence fits whole.

predict.question: if you double the chunk size from 40 to 80 words, the number of chunks…

feedback.right: right: the text is the same, so chunks twice as big give about half as many. Overlap shifts the math a bit, since each chunk repeats the end of the one before.
feedback.wrong: it roughly halves: same text, cut into bigger pieces. Overlap makes the math not exact.
feedback.skipped: no guess? Compare the chunk count at 40 and at 80.

coach.ui: guess noted. Move size from 40 to 80 and watch the chunk counter.
coach.cmd: guess noted. Run chunk --size 40 and then --size 80.

tryNext.ui: Now size 200: almost one chunk left. Search finds it, but the chunk sent to the LLM carries the whole handbook.
tryNext.cmd: Run chunk --size 200 and see the big-chunk warning.

why.simples:
For the AI to look up a handbook, we cut it into pieces, like index cards. A card too small can cut the answer sentence in half; one too big has everything mixed.
Overlap repeats the end of one card at the start of the next, so nothing gets lost at the seam.
why.dev:
Fixed-size chunking (in words or tokens) with overlap is the starting point. Better: split along structure (headings, paragraphs, list items) and only then cap the size.
Common sizes sit between 200 and 800 tokens with 10% to 20% overlap, but the right value depends on the questions: measure on a test set (the recall@k lesson) instead of copying a number.
why.especialista:
A chunk serves two uses pulling opposite ways: for embedding, small and single-topic gives sharper vectors; for the LLM, bigger gives context. One pattern indexes small chunks and returns the bigger "parent" passage (parent-child, or sentence window).
Store each chunk’s offset in the source document to cite and highlight it. When you change the chunking strategy, reindex everything and compare recall on the same set.

errors.aboveMax.size: Up to 400 words in this exercise.
errors.model.overlapTooBig: Overlap must be smaller than the chunk size, or the window never moves.

chunkTexts: Vacation must be requested through the employee portal 30 days in advance and needs the manager’s approval.
Vacation can be split into up to three periods: one of at least 14 days and the others of at least 5 days each.
Employees can sell up to one third of their vacation (cash allowance), asking together with the vacation request.
The meal allowance (VR) is R$ 45 per working day; anyone may swap it for the grocery allowance (VA) of the same value.
The health plan covers spouses and children up to 24 as dependents, with co-payment on appointments.
The PLR profit share is paid in March, proportional to how well company and team goals were met the previous year.
Remote work is allowed up to 2 days a week, agreed with the manager at the start of each month.
Anyone with remote days gets a R$ 120 monthly home office allowance, paid with the salary.
Work expenses are reimbursed with an invoice uploaded in the expenses app within 30 days.
Home internet and electricity aren’t reimbursable: those costs are already covered by the home office allowance.
To change your portal password, go to My profile > Security or call IT extension 4000.
To use the VPN, install the corporate app and select the AUR-VPN-02 profile.

steps: Take the clean text from the last lesson (or a document of yours) and write 5 questions with the exact answer sentence.
Split it into 50-, 200- and 800-word chunks with 10% overlap (LangChain RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter or a simple loop).
For each size, check that each answer sentence fits whole in some chunk.
recipe.ok: there’s a size where all 5 answers fit whole and each chunk covers a single topic. That’s your starting point.
